findings.evidence: Mathlib has no such lemma: `grep -rn "involute (ι" Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/` returns only unrelated hits in BaseChange.lean:113, Equivs.lean:148, SpinGroup.lean:114; Conjugation.lean:51 has only `involute_ι`. The PR's new file docstring itself frames the scope as the involution "usable as an odd operator alongside exterior multiplication and contraction", then records only the contraction side.
findings.fix: Add `theorem involute_ι_mul (m : M) (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) : involute (ι Q m * x) = -(ι Q m * involute x)` alongside `involute_contractLeft` in `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Contraction.lean`, and derive `parity_wedge` from it (or drop `parity_wedge` and rewrite with it directly at line 248).
findings.issue: `parity_wedge` proves `involute (ι x * s) = -(ι x * involute s)` only for `Q = 0` on `P.W`, but the proof (`map_mul` + `involute_ι` + `neg_mul`) uses nothing about the form or the module: the identity holds for `CliffordAlgebra Q` at arbitrary `Q`. This is exactly the multiplication half of the pair whose contraction half the PR does generalize, into `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Contraction.lean`; the general result is stated nowhere and only its special case survives.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/ExteriorAlgebra/Basic.lean:90 `ι_sq_zero`; Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Contraction.lean:188 `contractLeft_contractLeft (x) : d⌋(d⌋x) = 0`; Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Conjugation.lean:62 `involute_involute`. Repo-wide grep shows the only uses of all three are CliffordAction.lean:248-249.
findings.fix: Delete the three lemmas and rewrite line 248's simp set with the Mathlib names directly (`ExteriorAlgebra.ι_sq_zero`, `CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_contractLeft`, `CliffordAlgebra.involute_involute`), unfolding through `wedge_apply`/`contract_apply`/`parity_apply`.
findings.issue: `wedge_wedge` (187), `contract_contract` (191) and `parity_parity` (205) are public, docstring-advertised restatements of Mathlib lemmas at a strictly narrower level, each carrying a `SpinPolarizationData P` parameter it uses only through the module `P.W`. None has any polarization content, and all three are consumed only inside `cliffordOperator_sq`, so stating an operator fact about `⋀·N` now requires conjuring a whole polarization.

summary: The lift from the roadmap's ℂ-only pin to an arbitrary CommRing is the right level, and contract_wedge/parity_contract carry real polarization content. But four of the six anticommutators are Q=0/P.W specializations of facts that hold for every quadratic form or every module, exported publicly at the narrow level: parity_wedge hides a general Clifford lemma that the PR's own new general file is the natural home for, and three others merely restate Mathlib under a P parameter.
